plan.topic: Elecoglipron (AstraZeneca), an investigational once-daily small-molecule GLP-1 pill: how it works, what the VISTA Phase 2b trial showed (Lancet, June 2026: 310 adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition; 11.8% average weight loss at 36 weeks on the 75 mg arm vs 0.3% on placebo), the new fed vs fasted study (Br J Clin Pharmacol, Oct 19, 2026, healthy volunteers), and its dated Phase 3 status
plan.angle:
Lane P decoder (log 'lane: P'), series 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded'. 0–15 s: what viewers will know by the end, the first answer ('a once-daily GLP-1 pill that's still investigational, now in Phase 3') and a dated status. Chapters named as searched questions:
(1) What is elecoglipron?
(2) How is a small-molecule pill different from a peptide like oral semaglutide, and why does oral semaglutide have food and water rules? Cite the label wording.
(3) What did the Phase 2 trial show? Per-arm results vs placebo, group sizes, the estimand and 36 weeks, copied from the Lancet paper; the population stated exactly.
(4) Blood sugar results, only if the paper reports them, with the population for each.
(5) Side effects: GI rates per arm vs placebo and discontinuations, from the paper.
(6) Can you take it with food? What the fed vs fasted study measured. Healthy volunteers, Phase 1, pharmacokinetics only, not a weight result.
(7) Where it sits next to oral semaglutide and orforglipron: separate trials, not head-to-head, no ranking.
(8) What's next: Phase 3 trial names and dates from ClinicalTrials.gov or AstraZeneca releases. Investigational, not approved by the FDA, MHRA, Health Canada or TGA as of 26 Oct 2026.
No 'beat' frame. Re-hook every 45–75 s. One subscribe ask, after the trial payoff. Never online sources; for approved options or a clinical trial, ask a prescriber. Include 'Not personal advice', 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own' and the full prescriber line. End by naming the live long-form 'Orforglipron (Foundayo): The GLP-1 Pill With No Food Rules (US Label)'. 8–12 min, 14:00 ET.

package.description:
Elecoglipron is an investigational once-daily small-molecule GLP-1 pill from AstraZeneca, now in Phase 3. As of 26 October 2026 it isn't approved by the FDA, MHRA, Health Canada or TGA. In the Phase 2 VISTA trial (310 adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition), the group that worked up to 75 mg lost an average 10.5% of body weight at 26 weeks vs 0.6% on placebo (11.8% vs 0.3% at 36 weeks). The most common side effects were digestive, such as nausea.

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own.

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: Elecoglipron is an experimental GLP-1 receptor agonist from AstraZeneca. In plain words, it's a drug built to switch on the same switch as one of your gut hormones, and it comes as a small pill taken once a day.

visual.stock_query: pill key turning a glowing lock

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: To see why that matters, meet the hormone it copies. After you eat, cells in your gut release GLP-1, a messenger that tells your body food has arrived.

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: GLP-1 helps your pancreas release insulin when blood sugar is rising. It dials down glucagon, slows how fast your stomach empties, and sends fullness signals to the brain.
scenes.retention_device: Visual list, a new element on screen

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: That brain signalling is a big reason these medicines are studied for appetite and weight, not just blood sugar.

visual.stock_query: calm brain with a satisfied smile

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: But your own GLP-1 has a catch. An enzyme called D P P four chops it up fast. Intact GLP-1 lasts less than two minutes in your blood.

visual.stat_label: Half-life of your own intact GLP-1

scenes.section: What is elecoglipron?
scenes.narration: So every GLP-1 medicine is an engineering fix for that two-minute problem. The question is how you build the fix, and that's where pills get interesting.
scenes.on_screen_text: How do you build the fix?

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: Semaglutide is a peptide. That means it's a chain of amino acids, the same building blocks as the protein on your plate.

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: And your stomach is built to digest protein. Swallow a peptide and stomach enzymes start breaking it down, and its large size makes it hard to absorb.

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: Oral semaglutide, sold as Rybelsus for type two diabetes, gets around this with a helper molecule called SNAC. It protects the drug right where the tablet sits and helps it cross the stomach lining.

visual.stock_query: tiny bodyguard shielding pill in stomach

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: Even so, the US label estimates that only about zero point four to one percent of the semaglutide in each tablet reaches the bloodstream.
scenes.on_screen_text: Most of the dose never arrives

visual.stat_label: Oral semaglutide absolute bioavailability, US label

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: That's why the label is so precise. It says: take it at least thirty minutes before the first food, beverage, or other oral medications of the day, with no more than four ounces of plain water only.

visual.quote: Take RYBELSUS at least 30 minutes before the first food, beverage, or other oral medications of the day with no more than 4 ounces of plain water only.
visual.stock_query: label card beside small water glass

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: The label also warns that waiting less than thirty minutes, or taking it with food or drinks other than plain water, will lessen its effect by decreasing absorption.

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: So for someone like Marcus, who lives for that first coffee, the rule is a real part of the morning. If it's ever felt fussy to you, that's not you failing. It's chemistry.
scenes.retention_device: Validation, then back to the relatable thread

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: Elecoglipron takes a different route. It's a small molecule: a compact, non-peptide chemical, more like most everyday tablets, designed to switch on the same GLP-1 receptor.

visual.stock_query: small sleek key versus long chain

scenes.section: Why do some GLP-1 pills have food rules?
scenes.narration: Because it isn't a protein chain, it doesn't face the same stomach digestion or need a SNAC-style helper. But here's the twist: that doesn't automatically mean food has no effect. That has to be tested, and it was.

visual.stock_query: scientist holding pill and breakfast plate

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: What did the elecoglipron trial show?

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: The key study is called VISTA. It's a Phase two trial, published in The Lancet in June twenty twenty-six.

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: It included three hundred and ten adults with obesity, or with overweight plus at least one weight-related health condition.

visual.stat_label: Adults with obesity or overweight-related condition
visual.stock_query: diverse group of adults, friendly crowd

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: They were randomly assigned to different daily doses of elecoglipron or to a placebo pill. The placebo group matters, because simply joining a trial changes how people eat and move.

visual.stock_query: people sorted into colourful pill groups

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: The main result was measured at twenty-six weeks: ten point five percent average weight loss in the group that worked up to seventy-five milligrams, versus zero point six on placebo. People kept losing after that, so we'll follow them to thirty-six weeks, roughly eight months.

visual.stat_label: 75 mg arm (weekly step-up) vs 0.6% placebo, 26 weeks

scenes.retention_device: Primary result stated, then a forward loop to 36 weeks

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: Quick question for you. Between week twenty-six and week thirty-six, did the gap between the two groups shrink, or grow?

visual.stock_query: Marcus thinking, scale with question mark

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: At thirty-six weeks, the placebo group had lost an average of zero point three percent. For someone weighing two hundred and twenty pounds, that's less than a pound.

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: The group that worked up to seventy-five milligrams of elecoglipron lost an average of eleven point eight percent of their body weight at thirty-six weeks. So the gap grew.

visual.stat_label: Elecoglipron 75 mg arm: average weight loss, 36 weeks

scenes.retention_device: Big reveal, pays off the viewer question

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: For that same two-hundred-and-twenty-pound person, eleven point eight percent is about twenty-six pounds, roughly twelve kilograms. That's about the weight of a big bag of dog food.

visual.stock_query: big bag of dog food on scale

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: Two honest caveats. First, it's an average, so some people lost more and some lost less. Second, it's one dose group. The paper reports results for each dose separately.

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: And thirty-six weeks is a Phase two snapshot. Phase two is how researchers judge whether a drug works and which doses to carry forward. It can't tell us long-term results.

visual.myth: A Phase 2 result means it's ready
visual.fact: Phase 2 picks doses; Phase 3 tests at scale

scenes.section: What did the elecoglipron trial show?
scenes.narration: For Marcus, that brings two feelings at once. Hope, because eleven point eight versus zero point three is a big gap. And patience, because the bigger trials aren't finished.
scenes.retention_device: Emotional beat from the relatable thread

scenes.section: Does elecoglipron lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Since GLP-1 helps release insulin, it's a fair question. But VISTA was a weight trial in adults with obesity or overweight, without type two diabetes. A diabetes answer needs a diabetes trial in that population.

visual.stock_query: two doors labelled weight and diabetes

scenes.section: Does elecoglipron lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: And elecoglipron has one. In a separate Phase two b trial called SOLSTICE, in four hundred and six adults with type two diabetes, H b A one c, a measure of average blood sugar, fell by between zero point nine and one point nine percentage points across doses at twenty-six weeks, versus zero point one five on placebo.
scenes.on_screen_text: SOLSTICE (Phase 2b, type 2 diabetes): HbA1c down 0.9–1.9 pts vs 0.15 placebo, 26 wks

visual.stat_label: SOLSTICE, type 2 diabetes: HbA1c drop, 26 weeks
visual.stock_query: glucose meter needle easing down, calm

scenes.retention_device: Surprise payoff: the diabetes data exists

scenes.section: Does elecoglipron lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: It's still investigational, so if blood sugar is your main concern, approved type two diabetes medicines have years of data, and a prescriber can walk you through them.

scenes.section: What are elecoglipron's side effects?
scenes.narration: This is the part many people worry about most. GLP-1 medicines slow the stomach and act on appetite circuits, so their most common side effects are digestive.

scenes.section: What are elecoglipron's side effects?
scenes.narration: The oral semaglutide label, for example, lists the most common as nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, decreased appetite, vomiting and constipation.

scenes.section: What are elecoglipron's side effects?
scenes.narration: For elecoglipron, the VISTA paper reports digestive side effects for each dose against placebo, plus how many people stopped treatment. That dose-by-dose view is one reason Phase two tests several doses. In the food study too, the most common side effects were digestive, like nausea, vomiting and indigestion, and were mostly mild.

scenes.section: What are elecoglipron's side effects?
scenes.narration: If you've ever felt queasy on a medicine and wondered whether you were doing something wrong, you're not. It's a known effect, and it's worth raising with your prescriber rather than toughing it out alone.

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: On the nineteenth of October, twenty twenty-six, the British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology published a study comparing elecoglipron taken with food versus on an empty stomach.

visual.stock_query: two plates: full breakfast and empty

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: It was a Phase one study in healthy volunteers. Not a weight trial.

visual.myth: A food study shows weight results
visual.fact: Phase 1, healthy volunteers, blood levels only

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: It measured pharmacokinetics: how much drug reaches the blood, how fast, and how long it stays, with a meal compared with no meal.
scenes.on_screen_text: How much, how fast, how long

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: Think of it as checking whether breakfast changes how much of the pill gets through the door. That's the exact problem that shapes the rules for the peptide pill.

visual.stock_query: pill knocking on door, toast nearby

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: And here's the payoff of the thread we started with. The design choice is peptide versus small molecule. A peptide needs an empty stomach and a helper to get through.

visual.stock_query: long chain pill versus small key

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: A small molecule might not need that. But 'might' isn't evidence, so researchers test it with exactly this kind of study.

visual.stock_query: scientist weighing maybe on balance scale

scenes.retention_device: 'But, therefore' rhythm, sets up the finding

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: What did it find? In fourteen healthy volunteers given a single dose, the total amount of elecoglipron reaching the blood was very similar with a meal and without one, and the authors concluded it may be taken fed or fasted.
scenes.on_screen_text: Phase 1, 14 healthy volunteers, single dose: total exposure similar fed or fasted

visual.stock_query: two matching blood-level bars, toast and empty plate

scenes.retention_device: Main loop answered with the study's actual finding

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: What it can't tell you: whether weight loss changes with meals, or how a future label would tell people to take it. Those instructions come only after regulators review the full data.

visual.stock_query: blank label waiting for regulator stamp

scenes.retention_device: Sets honest limits right after the finding

scenes.section: Can you take elecoglipron with food?
scenes.narration: So for now, treat it as an encouraging but early check. It also shows the developers are asking a question that matters to real mornings like Marcus's.

scenes.section: How does elecoglipron compare to other GLP-1 pills?
scenes.narration: Elecoglipron isn't alone. Notice its ending, 'glipron'. It shares that with orforglipron, Lilly's small-molecule GLP-1 pill. In orforglipron's Phase two obesity trial, the most common side effects were also digestive, mostly mild to moderate.

scenes.section: How does elecoglipron compare to other GLP-1 pills?
scenes.narration: And oral semaglutide is the peptide pill we met earlier, with its thirty-minute rule.

scenes.section: How does elecoglipron compare to other GLP-1 pills?
scenes.narration: So can we rank them? No. They were tested in separate trials, with different people, doses and lengths of time. None of this is head-to-head.

scenes.section: How does elecoglipron compare to other GLP-1 pills?

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe overall. VISTA (Lancet, 2026; 310 adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without type 2 diabetes): 75 mg gave 10.5% versus 0.6% on placebo at the 26-week primary endpoint, and 11.8% versus 0.3% at 36 weeks. SOLSTICE (406 adults with type 2 diabetes): HbA1c fell 0.91 to 1.88 points versus 0.15 on placebo at 26 weeks. The food study (Br J Clin Pharmacol, 19 Oct 2026): Phase 1, 14 healthy volunteers randomized, similar exposure fed or fasted (AUC ratio about 0.96), authors say it "may be administered under fed or fasted conditions", and side effects were mostly mild and digestive (nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia). AstraZeneca's move to Phase 3 is confirmed: 9 Phase 3 trials are recruiting on ClinicalTrials.gov. The Rybelsus label claims (0.4–1% bioavailability, the 30-minute/4 oz rule, the common side effects) and the GLP-1 physiology (intact half-life under 2 minutes) are correct. The orforglipron Phase 2 side-effect statement matches the NEJM 2023 paper. The safety lines, "don't switch on your own", the investigational status, the "separate trials, not head-to-head" line and the hypothetical Marcus are all handled properly. There are three minor precision fixes. The most important: the VISTA paper's own title calls it 'phase 2', not '2b'. SOLSTICE is the 2b trial. Fetch note: PubMed, LifeScience, AstraZeneca and Drugs.com didn't load directly (PubMed showed only a cookie page; the others returned 403). Each record was confirmed through search results and secondary coverage, such as Healio, which loaded in full.

issues.claim: It's a Phase two b trial, published in The Lancet in June twenty twenty-six. / 'VISTA · Phase 2b · The Lancet'
issues.problem: The Lancet VISTA paper's title says 'a multicentre, phase 2, randomised, placebo-controlled clinical trial'. 'Phase 2b' is the label of the separate SOLSTICE paper. This mixes up the two trials.
issues.fix: Narration: "The key study is called VISTA. It's a Phase two trial, published in The Lancet in June twenty twenty-six." On-screen: "VISTA · Phase 2 · The Lancet"

issues.claim: ten point five percent average weight loss on seventy-five milligrams
issues.problem: Healio describes the 10.5% arm as '75 mg with weekly titration'. VISTA tested several dosing schedules, so the arm should be named exactly, per the channel's rule on exact arms. The numbers themselves are correct.
issues.fix: s29 narration: "...ten point five percent average weight loss in the group that worked up to seventy-five milligrams, versus zero point six on placebo." Change the s29 stat_label to "75 mg arm (weekly step-up) vs 0.6% placebo, 26 weeks". Optionally, the s32 stat_label can read "Elecoglipron 75 mg arm: average weight loss, 36 weeks".

issues.claim: In fourteen healthy volunteers, the amount of elecoglipron reaching the blood was very similar with a meal and without one
issues.problem: The study was a single 50 mg dose of two formulations (14 randomized, 13 completed). Saying 'a single dose' keeps the scope honest. Peak level (Cmax) varied more than total exposure (ratio 1.15, confidence interval 0.90–1.46).
issues.fix: Narration: "What did it find? In fourteen healthy volunteers given a single dose, the total amount of elecoglipron reaching the blood was very similar with a meal and without one, and the authors concluded it may be taken fed or fasted." On-screen: "Phase 1, 14 healthy volunteers, single dose: total exposure similar fed or fasted"

issues.claim: S2 URL (lifescience.net) and S14 (Healio) support the food study and SOLSTICE
issues.problem: Both are secondary records. The primary SOLSTICE Lancet paper exists (ScienceDirect PII S0140673626008020) and should be cited for the s40 numbers. Healio can stay as a supporting source.
issues.fix: Add a source: 'Elecoglipron, an oral small molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist in adults with type 2 diabetes (SOLSTICE): a multicentre, phase 2b, randomised, placebo-controlled trial', The Lancet, 2026, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0140673626008020. thumbnail.reasoning: All three are legible, but #0 pairs the strongest honest curiosity driver (a precise, concrete trial number — 11.8% — with a smiling pill character that visually represents the actual drug being explained) with a single clean focal point and high contrast (yellow on deep purple). It directly rewards the title's promise ('What Is Elecoglipron... Phase 3') without repeating its words, satisfying the playbook's thumbnail rule (≤4 words, one labelled character, no title repeat, one honest emotion). #1's question-mark-pill is a reasonable curiosity hook but is more generic and less tied to the specific news value of the video. #2's heart mascot is a content mismatch (a pill/drug explainer shown with a heart character) and includes an odd floating circled element near the top that looks like an unresolved asset glitch, hurting both polish and topical relevance. #0 best balances CTR potential and clean execution without misleading claims — the number is sourced from the video's own trial data per the headline logic.
